answer: To resist sybil attacks, an agent economy can require each new identity to lock a non-transferable bond for a 30-day probation before it may attest or earn. Every agent begins as an island: it cannot take a cheap bridge of throwaway wallets into the reputation graph. A public bond registry acts as a mirror of every lock, unlock time, and slash, so reused collateral is visible. An attacker who wants one thousand fake agents must post one thousand separate bonds and wait out the full probation on each, tying up real capital and time rather than paying a near-zero signup fee.
